title: Canonical comparison of the Kan image triangle with denominator values
statement: Let $D,D^{\prime}$ be triangulated categories [def-weil-triangulated-category], $L$ a category with integer shifts, $F:D\to D^{\prime}$ exact, and $S$ a saturated triangulated multiplicative system [def-pur-saturated-triangulated-localization]. Let $Q:D\to L$ be a shift-compatible localization and $LF:L\to D^{\prime}$ a shift-compatible right Kan extension of $F$ with shift-compatible counit $\alpha:Q\circ LF\to F$. Assume all structured-arrow diagrams for this Kan extension have limits. Let $T=(X,Y,Z,f,g,h)$ be any triangle of $D$, not necessarily distinguished. For $U=X,Y,Z$, let $L_U$ be a left-derived value and $u_U$ a witnessing cone on its denominator diagram, with a stage $s_0$ and retraction $r$ such that $u_U(s_0)r=1$, and every transition to a stage $s$ factors at a common earlier stage through $r$ and $u_U(s)$. Suppose maps $l_f:L_X\to L_Y$, $l_g:L_Y\to L_Z$, $l_h:L_Z\to L_X[1]$ satisfy $u_X(s)F(f^{\prime})=l_fu_Y(s^{\prime})$ whenever $sf=f^{\prime}s^{\prime}$, and $u_Y(s)F(g^{\prime})=l_gu_Z(s^{\prime})$ whenever $sg=g^{\prime}s^{\prime}$; for the last map suppose $u_Z(s)F(h^{\prime})=l_h u_X(s^{\prime})[1](F\text{ shift comparison})^{-1}$ whenever $sh=h^{\prime}s^{\prime}[1]$. Then there is a triangle isomorphism $(Q\circ LF)(T)\cong(L_X,L_Y,L_Z,l_f,l_g,l_h)$. No distinguishedness conclusion is asserted.

proof.text: Compare each supplied denominator value with the pointwise Kan extension using the structured-arrow bridge and cone uniqueness; Mathlib isPointwiseRightKanExtensionOfIsRightKanExtension identifies the given global right Kan extension with its pointwise limit because pointwise limits exist everywhere. No total-derived-functor construction is used.

For the first two maps, right fractions give denominator squares. The fraction identity, naturality of alpha, and the supplied equations identify the maps after the value isomorphisms; split-mono cancellation from the chosen retractions closes each square.
For the third map, shift the first denominator by S shift invariance, use the shift compatibility of alpha and F, and apply the analogous fraction square and split-mono cancellation.
The three value isomorphisms and their three commutative squares form Triangle.isoMk, yielding the claimed triangle isomorphism.

proof_origin.place: Value-identification step in Proposition 05SE; proved by cone uniqueness, fraction squares and split-mono cancellation, with shifted naturality for the third map
